## 👹 Horde — From the Wound, We Rise.

The **Banished** trace their origin to a forgotten fracture — a place where laws failed, curses lingered, and survival demanded transformation. Those cast out or altered by forbidden forces gathered there, not by choice, but by necessity.

Orcs, cursed and banished souls, and beings reshaped by unnatural powers found kinship not through comfort, but through shared endurance. What could not be healed was mastered. What could not be forgiven was carried.

They did not ask to return.
They learned to persist.

‎ ‎ ‎
‎ ‎ ‎

### The Great Breach
Thirteen years ago, during what records now call **The Great Breach**, the world split where an ancient ward failed. Among the Horde, this moment is remembered simply as **the Wound** — a living fracture that bled corruption into land and flesh alike. Those closest were not all destroyed — many were changed, marked by curse and unnatural endurance.

When the world withdrew to contain the damage, paths were sealed and the altered left behind. From those lawless days came ritual scars, crimson markings, and the first weapon rites. The Horde believes the Wound still listens, answering not to prayer, but to will, rage, and sacrifice.

The axe upon red marks the moment waiting ended. The world turned away — and the Horde learned to move forward without it.

‎ ‎ ‎
‎ ‎ ‎

### The Horde Way
The Horde believes that exile reveals truth, and that pain is a teacher rather than a curse. Power is not given, only taken and mastered. Survival is not shameful — it is proof. Corruption, when bound by will, becomes strength, and forgiveness from the world is neither expected nor required.

The Banished do not seek absolution.
They endure — and in enduring, they define themselves.

‎ ‎ ‎
‎ ‎ ‎

‎ ‎ ‎ “We are not what the Wound did to us. We are what we chose to carry.”

‎ ‎ ‎ — **Buzz**
